title: Debt servicing, weak private-sector credit pressuring Bangladesh: DCCI
summary:
High debt-servicing costs, weak private-sector credit and inflation are putting pressure on Bangladesh, the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry said. 
However, recent business-facilitation reforms could boost investment and job creation, it said. 
To address fiscal vulnerabilities, it suggested limiting domestic bank borrowing, accelerating NBR digitalisation and tightening borrowing discipline.

title: China sees growth in new foreign-invested firms in Jan-Jul 2026
summary:
China saw a rise in newly established foreign-invested enterprises and robust growth in FDI in high-tech industries in the first seven months this year despite a drop in overall inflows. 
During the period, 37,711 such new enterprises were set up—up by 4.4 per cent YoY, while FDI in actual use came in at $64.63 billion—down by 6.2 per cent YoY. 
Manufacturing attracted $16.28 billion in FDI.

title: China, Uzbekistan agree to expand textile sector cooperation
summary:
China and Uzbekistan have agreed to expand textile sector cooperation, including in raw material supplies, technology, investment and the creation of joint production units. 
The talks took place in Aral in China’s Xinjiang. 
Uzbek firms discussed supplies of synthetic and chemical fibres with China. 
Both sides considered cooperation in production of blended fabrics and automation of production processes.

title: Canada suspends trade negotiations with US
summary:
Canada has suspended trade negotiations with the US and directed its negotiators to return to Ottawa. 
“…Last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic and called into question the reliability of any deal,” PM Mark Carney said. 
The US has imposed a 50-per cent tariff on roughly $28 billion worth Canadian goods.   
Canada will match those tariffs ‘dollar for dollar’, he said.

title: China drives 12.5% rise in Brazil’s cotton exports in H1 2026
summary:
Brazil’s raw cotton exports rose 12.5 per cent year on year to $2.793 billion in January–June 2026, supported by supplies, pricing, fibre quality and traceability.
China became the top market as shipments surged 160.1 per cent to $608.045 million, while Bangladesh rose 18.9 per cent. 
Top five markets made up 79.41 per cent; Brazil is forecast to remain the largest exporter in 2026–27.

title: Philippines fiscal consolidation slows amid weak growth: Fitch Ratings
summary:
The Philippines’ proposed 2027 budget targets a deficit of 5.1 per cent of GDP, signalling slower fiscal consolidation amid weak growth, Fitch Ratings said. 
GDP grew just 2.3 per cent YoY in Q2 2026. Fitch expects medium-term growth of around 6 per cent, while lower revenue expectations and reduced infrastructure spending could weigh on the fiscal outlook and debt stabilisation.

title: Global growth remains resilient amid rising H2 risks: Report
summary:
Nomura says global growth stayed resilient in the first half of 2026 despite energy shocks, inflation and higher yields, backed by AI and policy.
US and euro area demand remains supported for sourcing, but oil-price and Middle East risks may lift costs and hit sentiment.
Asia is uneven: AI demand favours Greater China, South Korea, Malaysia and Singapore; China has weak demand but strong exports.

title: IATA CEC 2026 to focus on improving air cargo operations
summary:
IATA’s 2026 Cargo Experts Conference (CEC), scheduled for September 23-24 in Budapest, will focus on improving air cargo operations through global standards, technology and data. 
Three specialised tracks will cover Digital Cargo, Safety and Security, and Pharma and Cargo Operations, addressing AI, automation, lithium battery risks, ground handling and cold-chain resilience.

title: France’s economic index edges up 0.1% in June: TCB
summary:
France’s LEI rose 0.1 per cent to 111.7 in June 2026, slowing from a 0.4 per cent increase in May. 
The LEI gained 1.4 per cent in H1 2026, compared with 1.8 per cent in H2 2025. 
The CEI was unchanged at 111.0 in June after rising 0.1 per cent in May, while it edged up 0.2 per cent during H1 2026, signalling broadly stable current economic conditions.

title: UK businesses face supply-chain, trade & workforce pressures: ONS
summary:
UK businesses faced continued pressure from economic uncertainty, labour costs and energy prices in August 2026. 
Office for National Statistics (ONS) data showed turnover broadly stable, while 61 per cent expressed concern over energy prices. 
Supply-chain disruption and international conflict also remained key risks, although 94 per cent of businesses continued trading.

title: Could Kenya become Egypt’s gateway to a wider African market?
summary:
Africa’s young, urbanising consumer base is creating sustained demand for apparel and footwear. 
Egypt’s ECAHT has agreed to set up a logistics hub in Kenya to reduce freight costs, delivery times and distributor access barriers. 
The hub will cover shipping, warehousing and insurance, with shipments due in September and targeted garment exports estimated to rise by at least 20 per cent.

title: Do Bangladesh’s apparel exports to the EU face a tougher road ahead?
summary:
Bangladesh’s apparel exports to the EU fell 16.43 per cent to €8.64 billion in January-June 2026, steepest amongst key suppliers. 
EU apparel imports weakened, but lower unit prices kept Bangladesh’s higher volumes from raising value. 
LDC graduation uncertainty, possible EU-India FTA gains, energy shortages and Chinese and Vietnamese marketing press suppliers on reliability and value addition.

title: Japan’s apparel imports increase 10% in July 2026
summary:

Textile yarn and fabric imports climbed 20.1 per cent, while exports rose 14.6 per cent and textile machinery exports 17.7 per cent. 
First-half 2026 apparel imports increased 6.0 per cent; textile machinery outbound shipments grew 11.7 per cent to 160,129 million yen.

title: EU packaging law goes live: The 35% question apparel cannot ignore
summary:
EU PPWR has generally applied since August 12, 2026, but apparel exporters face staggered compliance, not one deadline.
Immediate work centres on documentation, operator responsibility and packaging-data visibility for polybags, cartons and mailers.
Redesign accelerates towards 2028–30 as EU sourcing shifts, with Vietnam and China gaining while Bangladesh and Türkiye fall.

title: US apparel brands limit value decline to 1% in 2026
summary:
US retained the largest presence in the Apparel 50 2026 ranking, with 12 brands valued at a combined $68.8 billion.
Their value slipped 1 per cent, versus a 4 per cent fall for the global top 50 to $350.9 billion.
Nike stayed third globally, while Tiffany & Co. led US growth and Levi’s drew attention with World Cup marketing.
Retail sourcing teams gain a benchmark on demand resilience.

title: Germany’s Puma confirms VP Johan Adamsson’s exit after 25 years
summary:

title: Bangladesh opens MSME registration for tax, business benefits
summary:

Registered SMEs can claim turnover-based tax exemptions; thresholds are higher for women and entrepreneurs with disabilities. 
Certificates enable annual overseas business remittances of up to $3,000 and access to fairs, export training, easier loans and matchmaking.

title: 39% gone; yet fast fashion still can’t quit China
summary:
TexPro shows US core-garment imports from China fell 41.4 per cent to $2.73 billion in January–May 2026, a loss of about $1.93 billion.
China’s share dropped to 9.5 per cent; Vietnam gained only about $47 million, Cambodia $203 million and Indonesia $96 million.
Buyers are splitting risk, but China’s fabric, trims, labour and logistics ecosystem remains hard to reproduce for ultra-fast fashion.

title: Africa's US apparel loss could shift orders towards Asian suppliers
summary:
AGOA offers eligible sub-Saharan African countries duty-free US access for over 1,800 products until December 31, 2026.
Without extension, African apparel would lose AGOA preference and face US apparel duties plus any country-specific duties.
US clothing imports from Lesotho fell 76 per cent year on year in May 2026; short-staple spinning spindle shipments to Africa fell 46 per cent in 2025.

title: Italy defies decline in Hong Kong apparel imports on luxury demand
summary:

China remained the largest supplier at $1.238 billion, while Vietnam rose 6.9 per cent and France surged 28.0 per cent.
